text: Two agents, one goal, one simulated world. Then reality changes.
At tick six, route R1 closes. KEEL finds the step that assumed R1 was open, keeps the three finished steps, and repairs only the rest, with a recorded model proposal it validates live.
The static agent drives on, and learns too late.
Every number here is recomputed from the event log.
A failover target degrades. KEEL re-checks before shifting traffic, and moves checkout to region C.
The static plan sends checkout into the degraded region, and still reports success. KEEL never served an error.
Now a forged report, and a flapping sensor. The forgery is rejected. When the readings oscillate, KEEL pauses, and asks an operator.
One confirmation, and KEEL delivers. The naive agent followed the noise onto a closed road.
Crash the agent mid-step. It rebuilds from its persisted log: finished work kept, no effect applied twice.
Tested on SQLite and Postgres, in the browser, and under kill-and-takeover. All of it simulated.
KEEL. The plan can change. The goal stays.
